paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Distribution of articles across political leanings of the outlets
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of articles across four categories based on the political leanings of the media outlets, as analyzed in the paper “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse.” The chart is divided into four colored segments: “Right bias” (blue, 30.0%, n=30), “Left bias” (orange, 28.0%, n=28), “Questionable source” (green, 22.0%, n=22), and “Left center bias” (red, 20.0%, n=20). Each segment is labeled with its category name, percentage, and absolute count in parentheses. The segments are arranged clockwise starting from the top-right, with “Right bias” being the largest slice and “Left center bias” the smallest. The chart includes no legend, as labels are placed directly adjacent to each slice, and no slices are exploded or emphasized visually beyond their proportional size. The overall distribution suggests a slight predominance of right-leaning outlets, followed closely by left-leaning ones, with smaller shares attributed to questionable sources and left-center outlets.
